Services Impacts
Severe negative impacts such as deficiencies in school, health, public protection and municipal services as well as shortages in business services are likely to be felt for at least several years following major developments. This will occur before the public and private services can be expanded to meet the demand created by a rapidly increasing population. After this trying adjustment period, the impact is expected to be effectively mitigated.
Hardin will be the focal point of socio-economic impacts, although the Reservation communities of Crow Agency and Lodge Grass will also be affected. Municipal services, particularly sewage facilities, and housing are expected to be the areas of most immmediate concern.
Recreation
The major impact on recreation will result from increased population and the associated increase in demand for recreation. This increased pressure may cause land owners to close and post private land. This may result in overuse of existing facilities; some deterioration of available recreational resources on and near the project area is unavoidable. However, in view of the total potential, this should be minimal if good management of the recreation resources is practiced.
Another adverse impact will result from the unavoidable loss of land base suitable for certain recreational purposes.
Accidents
A net increase in numbers of accidents can be expected because of increases in population, automobile traffic and mining activity, although a decreased accident rate is expected to result from safety programs and devices.
